android.desc: You can’t always talk. They’re at work, on a flight, asleep in another time zone. Lune keeps you close through those hours. Your partner lives on your home screen: a whisper from them, how their day is going, a touch you can feel. Nothing to open, nothing to answer. Let them know you’re thinking of them You think of them in the middle of the day, but a text would start a conversation neither of you has time for. Send a whisper instead. It waits on their home screen until you send the next one, and they don’t owe you a reply. • Up to 60 characters, so it stays small. • End-to-end encrypted: only the two of you can read it. Know they’re okay, without calling The flight lands, the shift ends, the drive is over. One tap from them, and you get a gentle notification: “Sara landed”. • Home safe, Landed, All good, On my way, or words of their own. • Their status and mood sit on your widget: Busy, Commuting, Loved, Tired, or whatever they write. • A status can end on its own (“Busy until 6 pm”), and one that’s a day old fades, so you can tell what’s current. • Their battery is there too, for the nights you wonder why they went quiet. When words aren’t enough, reach for them Some days you just want to be near them. Send a touch and their phone answers with a soft pulse, while your moon glows on their screen. • A tap, a hold, or a heartbeat, each easy to tell apart by feel. • Decide together what each touch means: a hold for “miss you”, a heartbeat for “goodnight”. A small language only you two know. • Reach for each other in the same minute, and something rare happens. Stay close in one tap When you only have a second, the widget is enough. Set your status or mood, send a touch, or check in, without opening the app. Always know what time it is for them In a long-distance relationship, you do the math before every message. The widget does it for you: “Sara · late night”. And if it’s 2 am for them while you’re writing, you’ll see a quiet note before you send. • Your time zone is shared only while you choose to share it. A quiet place, just for you two Open Lune and their moon is waiting in a slow, moving sky: a starry night, a meadow full of fireflies, open water at dusk. A calm minute with them, whenever you need one. • Six scenes, at night and at dusk, with more on the way. • Pick the moon your partner sees you as, from eight colors. quotes.text:
Hello HN.

I built my first serious mobile (OS - Android) application, Lune. Before I tell you about it, I wanna tell you the backstory in short:

One day I woke up from a bad dream and had an instant anxiety attack (I don't get those easily). I needed to call someone I love in that moment, but it wasn't practical given the time of the day. I just needed a way to feel that person's presence. In that moment, the idea behind Lune was born (currently I've pivoted from the original idea a bit though :).

The thing is, as we get busier with our lives, it becomes increasingly difficult to stay meaningfully connected with our partner, texts can sit unread for hours, calls can become impractical for all kinds of reasons.

If we feel something, how do we express it without starting a call or a chat conversation? How do we express a feeling in a way that stays with our partner, without demanding a reply? So I thought what if I could whisper my subtle feelings, so that my partner doesn't have to a reply and feel that whisper whenever they got the time.

Before I list the features and explain why I picked them, I want to explain the name, Lune:

Lune means Moon in French. No matter where you're from in this world, you've certainly felt the calm, ambient presence of a glowing moon on a dark night. It gives us a sense of belonging and closeness.
